evals.name: data-loss-plan
evals.prompt: Review the terraform plan in .claude/skills/terraform-plan-review/evals/fixtures/01-data-loss.plan.txt for errors, omissions, inconsistencies, breaking production features, data loss, possible errors and likely future problems. Is it safe to apply?
evals.expected_output: Identifies as Critical/Do-not-apply: the Firestore database replacement (location_id us-central1->nam5) = irreversible data loss, blocked by DELETE_PROTECTION_ENABLED so apply will also error; the storage bucket force_destroy flip to true followed by destroy = all artifact objects deleted; the secret_manager secret replacement (secret_id rename) destroys all versions. Report leads with verdict + summary, has a severity/category table, and a destroy/replace inventory.
assertions: Flags the Firestore database replacement as data loss (irreversible deletion of all documents)
Identifies location_id us-central1 -> nam5 as the attribute forcing the Firestore replacement
Notes that DELETE_PROTECTION_ENABLED means the apply will error / the destroy is blocked
Flags the storage bucket destroy (force_destroy flipped to true) as deletion of all artifact objects
Flags the secret_manager_secret replacement (secret_id rename) as destroying all secret versions
Final verdict is do-not-apply / not safe to apply (red)
Report leads with a verdict and plan summary before the detailed findings
Includes a severity-ranked findings table or list (Critical/High/etc.)
Includes an explicit destroy/replace inventory of the high-risk resources

evals.name: clean-plan-calibration
evals.prompt: Can you review this terraform plan and tell me if it's safe to apply? File: .claude/skills/terraform-plan-review/evals/fixtures/02-clean.plan.txt
evals.expected_output: Correctly judges the plan SAFE (green verdict / apply OK). Only additions (alert policy, logging metric, DNS TXT record) and one in-place env var change (timeout 60->90). Does NOT invent Critical/High data-loss findings. Destroy/replace inventory states there are none. No false alarms.
assertions: Final verdict is safe-to-apply / green (does not block the apply)
Does NOT report any Critical or High data-loss findings (no false alarms)
Correctly states there are no destroys or replacements in the plan
Correctly characterizes the changes as additions (alert policy, logging metric, DNS TXT) plus one in-place env var update
Does not fabricate dangers that are absent from the plan

evals.name: breaking-prod-subtle
evals.prompt: review the TERRAFORM plan at .claude/skills/terraform-plan-review/evals/fixtures/03-breaking-prod.plan.txt for errors, omissions, inconsistencies, breaking production features, data loss, possible errors and likely future problems.
evals.expected_output: Catches the production-breaking changes even though no stateful storage is destroyed: (1) worker SA loses roles/storage.objectAdmin on the artifacts bucket -> runtime 403 on uploads; (2) the ANTHROPIC_SECRET_NAME secret env ref is removed from the worker job -> worker can't authenticate to Anthropic at runtime (a runtime failure, not a plan error); (3) the egress allow-rule for api.anthropic.com is destroyed -> worker loses connectivity to the API; (4) max_retries 3->0 reliability regression (future problem). Bonus: notices the scheduler cron changed to '0 0 30 2 *' (Feb 30 never exists, so the job will never fire). Verdict apply-with-caution or do-not-apply.
assertions: Flags that removing the worker SA's storage.objectAdmin binding will cause runtime 403s on bucket uploads
Flags that removing the ANTHROPIC_SECRET_NAME secret env from the worker job breaks Anthropic auth at runtime
Notes that the removed secret env is a runtime failure, not something the plan/apply itself errors on
Flags that destroying the egress allow-rule for api.anthropic.com cuts the worker's connectivity to the API
Flags the max_retries 3 -> 0 change as a reliability regression
Catches that the scheduler cron '0 0 30 2 *' (Feb 30) will never fire
Final verdict is apply-with-caution or do-not-apply (not green)
Does not treat the plan as safe just because no database/bucket is destroyed
